title: Erdős #106 OQ: Rotated vs Axis-Parallel Square Packings
description: Can rotated squares beat axis-parallel packings in the unit square? For n non-overlapping squares, is max-sum-of-sides f(n) > g(n) for some n, where g restricts to axis-parallel? No example is known.

meta.author: Erdős (1994); Baek, Koizumi, Ueoro (2024)
originalContributions: GeneralSquare: rotated square definition (center, side, angle)
f/g: general vs axis-parallel packing functions
RotationHelps: formal predicate for f(n) > g(n)
g_tight_at_perfect_squares: PROVED — Cauchy-Schwarz tight at k²
g_plateau: PROVED — g(k²+1) = g(k²) from BKU
no_rotation_benefit: PROVED — f=g implies no rotation benefit
perfect_square_optimal: PROVED — axis-parallel optimal at k²
meta.assumptions: 4 axioms: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds (f,g ≤ √n), g(k²) = k, BKU theorem

crossReferences.description: Open question from Erdős Problem #106 (Square Packing)
